title: Finite-type algebraic stacks over a field have affine smooth presentations
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $\mathcal Z$ be an algebraic stack over $k$: a stack in groupoids for etale coverings, with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a representable smooth surjective atlas from a scheme. Stacks, representability and 2-fibre products have the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; schemes and algebraic spaces use [def-pc-scheme, def-trf-algebraic-space]. Suppose $\mathcal Z$ is of finite type over $k$, meaning locally of finite type as tested on smooth scheme atlases, and quasi-compact. Here quasi-compact means that every cover of $\mathcal Z$ by open substacks has a finite subcover; an open substack is a full pullback-stable subcategory whose pullback to every scheme is an open subscheme. There exist an affine scheme $A$ of finite type over $k$ and a representable smooth surjective morphism $a:A\to\mathcal Z$. If $\mathcal Z$ is smooth over $k$, then $A$ is smooth over $k$. Smoothness and finite type on schemes mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; on stacks smoothness is tested on smooth atlases. A representable smooth surjective atlas means that after every scheme base change it is a smooth surjective morphism of algebraic spaces, tested on etale scheme charts. The empty stack and the empty affine scheme are allowed.

source.place: Tag 04YC (lemma-quasi-compact-stack), especially proof choosing a finite affine subcover of an atlas. Finite-type refinement: stacks-morphisms.tex Tag 06FS (definition-locally-finite-type); smooth refinement: Tag 075U (definition-smooth). The same affine-subcover proof applies to the etale-stack convention.

proof.text: Choose a representable smooth surjective scheme atlas $p:U\to\mathcal Z$. By the hypothesis that local finite type is tested on smooth atlases, $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type. Thus the definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] supplies an affine open cover $(U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i)_{i\in I}$ of $U$, each $B_i$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-atlas-open-image] to each $U_i\subseteq U$, obtaining open substacks $\mathcal W_i\subseteq\mathcal Z$ and smooth maps $U_i\to\mathcal Z$ which factor as smooth surjections onto $\mathcal W_i$.

source.place: Tag 04YC (lemma-quasi-compact-stack), proof of (1) implies (2), with Tag 05UP (lemma-open-image-substack) for the open image.

proof.text: The $\mathcal W_i$ cover $\mathcal Z$: after a scheme base change $T\to\mathcal Z$, their pullbacks are the images of the $U_i\times_{\mathcal Z}T\to T$, by [lem-sfb-smooth-atlas-open-image]. The $U_i$ cover $U$, and $U\times_{\mathcal Z}T\to T$ is surjective by the atlas hypothesis, so these images cover $T$. Quasi-compactness in the statement now gives a finite subset $J\subseteq I$ for which the $\mathcal W_j$ still cover. This uses exactly the given open-substack definition of quasi-compactness.

source.place: Tag 04YC (lemma-quasi-compact-stack), proof of (1) implies (2), with Tag 05UP (lemma-open-image-substack) for the open image.

proof.text: Form $A=\coprod_{j\in J}U_j$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. The objects $U_j\to\mathcal Z$ glue on this disjoint open cover to an object $a:A\to\mathcal Z$: on each self-overlap use the identity isomorphism, and on each overlap of distinct components use the unique empty-overlap isomorphism. These satisfy the cocycle condition [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum], $A\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_{j\in J}B_j)$, hence $A$ is affine. Its finite affine open cover by the $U_j$, with each $B_j$ finitely generated over $k$, is precisely the finite-cover criterion for $A$ to be of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Tag 04YC (lemma-quasi-compact-stack), proof of (1) implies (2), with Tag 05UP (lemma-open-image-substack) for the open image.

proof.text: The map $a$ is representable by algebraic spaces: for a scheme $T\to\mathcal Z$, its 2-fibre product with $A$ is the base change of the representable diagonal along $A\times_kT\to\mathcal Z\times_k\mathcal Z$. This is the groupoid of triples $(x,t,\phi:a(x)\simeq t)$ in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; the scheme product exists by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The coprojections $U_j\to A$ form a disjoint open cover [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Each restriction $U_j\to\mathcal Z$ is smooth by Step 1, so source-open locality in [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] proves that $a$ is smooth. For any scheme $T\to\mathcal Z$, put $A_T=A\times_{\mathcal Z}T$ and $T_j=T\times_{\mathcal Z}\mathcal W_j$. Pulling back the open cover of $A$ gives the open cover $U_j\times_{\mathcal Z}T$ of $A_T$: an object over a scheme belongs to its $j$-th member exactly when its $A$-coordinate factors through $U_j$. The $T_j$ cover $T$ by Step 2. The map $U_j\times_{\mathcal Z}T\to T$ has image exactly $T_j$ by [lem-sfb-smooth-atlas-open-image]. Every point of $T$ therefore lies in the image of a member of the cover of $A_T$, proving that $A_T\to T$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 04YC (lemma-quasi-compact-stack), proof of (1) implies (2), with Tag 05UP (lemma-open-image-substack) for the open image.

proof.text: If $\mathcal Z$ is smooth over $k$, the smooth-atlas test in the statement, applied to the smooth surjective atlas $A\to\mathcal Z$ just constructed, says exactly that $A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth. If $\mathcal Z$ is empty choose the empty atlas and $J=\varnothing$; the finite-coproduct spectrum identification gives $A=\operatorname{Spec}(0)$, the empty affine scheme. The finite-cover criterion and the smooth-atlas test also include this empty case.
